upper and lower bound above; DWWrappers::init places DWRichPresenceService at +0x1C8, sibling of DWCounter at +0x1B8

structs.notes: Replay offset of DWCounter inside DWWrappers is +0x1B8 (game-test +0x220). DWWrappers::init stores the owner at +8 of each embedded wrapper (DWCounter::init, DWMatchMaking::init); the IDA struct DWWrappers has no DWCounter member (packet embedded_in empty). The size is proven from the sibling offsets in DWWrappers::init, which is Replay evidence, not from the parent's rebuilt size. Proposal: apply the 16-byte size only together with the DWWrappers owner's layout (the slot after +0x1B8 must be DWRichPresenceService at +0x1C8).

structs.name: bdEventLogID

unconfirmed: m_eventLogID (+32, unsigned __int64): game-test offset; no Replay access. The Replay event path that handles event IDs uses different layouts: bdEventLog::recordEventsMixed@0x14212DE00 reads 4-byte event types at events+36 with an 72-byte element stride (`v13 += 18` DWORDs), DWEventLog::recordEventsMixed@0x140F75A80 takes the bdEventLog object from DWLobbyService::getEventLog, dwRecordEventInternal@0x141504300 calls DWEventLog::recordEventsMixed with no bdEventLogID object.

baseclass_0 / baseclass_10 (bdTaskResult, bdSerializable): see bdFileID; the Replay record object dwRecordEventObject_ctor@0x1420FB1B0 has these bases but writes a bool at +32, so it does not hold an 8-byte m_eventLogID at +32.
structs.notes: Left as partial, same reason as bdFileID. dwRecordEvent@0x141503F10 and dwRecordEventInternal@0x141504300 are the Replay counterparts of the game-test dwRecordEvent family that uses bdEventLogID; the Replay versions do not take this struct. Absence is likely but not proven.
